definition: Directly controlling reasoning length at inference: capping thinking tokens, or forcing continued deliberation by suppressing the end-of-thinking token (the "wait" trick).
details: Directly controlling reasoning length at inference: capping thinking tokens, or forcing continued deliberation by suppressing the end-of-thinking token (the "wait" trick). The product knob that trades latency and cost against accuracy per query.

explainer.lead: Budget forcing is a way to control how long an AI model deliberates before answering. It can stop reasoning at a token limit or make it continue, letting each query trade accuracy against response time and compute cost.

tiers.eli5: Imagine telling someone, "You have two minutes to solve this puzzle," or, when they stop early, "Wait—check it again." Budget forcing does something similar with an AI's thinking: it sets a limit or asks it to keep going. More thinking may help, but it also takes longer and costs more.
tiers.practitioner: At inference, set a per-query thinking-token budget and stop generation when it is exhausted, or suppress the end-of-thinking token and insert a continuation such as "Wait" to extend deliberation. Tune the budget against measured accuracy, latency, and cost. A hard cap can cut off useful reasoning, while forced continuation can spend tokens without improving the answer.
tiers.paperLevel: Let B be the thinking-token budget and L the number of reasoning tokens generated. Budget forcing directly controls L at inference: terminate deliberation when L reaches B, or suppress the end-of-thinking token so generation continues beyond the model's initial stopping point, typically with a "Wait" continuation. It changes test-time compute without changing model weights; additional deliberation is not guaranteed to improve accuracy.

explainer.example: For a difficult math query, a system allows 2,000 thinking tokens. If the model tries to finish after 800 tokens, the system suppresses that stopping signal and inserts "Wait", prompting further checking; if deliberation reaches 2,000 tokens, it is capped and the model answers.
explainer.intuition: A reasoning model may stop before doing enough checking, or keep thinking after extra tokens would add little value. Budget forcing treats deliberation length as a control knob rather than leaving it entirely to the model.
howItWorks: Send the query and choose a thinking-token budget.
Let the model generate its reasoning normally.
If the budget is exhausted, end thinking and produce the answer.
To extend thinking, suppress the end-of-thinking token and add a continuation such as "Wait".
Compare accuracy, latency, and cost to choose the budget.
explainer.whyItMatters: It makes test-time compute adjustable per query instead of fixed. That gives applications a direct way to balance answer quality against how long users wait and how much each request costs.
misconceptions: A larger budget does not guarantee a better answer.
Budget forcing controls inference-time deliberation; it does not retrain the model.
The token cap limits generated thinking, not necessarily the difficulty of the problem.

nodes.label: Final answer
nodes.note: Produced when deliberation ends or is capped.

diagram.caption: The controller either ends deliberation at the budget or forces another round of thinking.
